message: Ingest historical Area Health Resource Files

info.long_name: Health Professional Shortage Area Designation — Primary Care
info.short_description: Federal HPSA designation indicating primary care provider shortages.
info.long_description: Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designation for primary medical care, assigned by HRSA. A value of 1 indicates a whole-county shortage area; 2 indicates a partial-county shortage area; 0 or missing indicates no shortage designation. Whole-county HPSAs are eligible for federal programs including National Health Service Corps placements and J-1 visa waivers.
info.statement: In {location}, the primary care HPSA designation is {value}.

info.long_name: Health Professional Shortage Area Designation — Dental
info.short_description: Federal HPSA designation indicating dental provider shortages.
info.long_description: Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designation for dental care, assigned by HRSA. A value of 1 indicates a whole-county shortage area; 2 indicates a partial-county shortage area; 0 or missing indicates no shortage designation.
info.statement: In {location}, the dental HPSA designation is {value}.

info.long_name: Health Professional Shortage Area Designation — Mental Health
info.short_description: Federal HPSA designation indicating mental health provider shortages.
info.long_description: Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designation for mental health care, assigned by HRSA. A value of 1 indicates a whole-county shortage area; 2 indicates a partial-county shortage area; 0 or missing indicates no shortage designation.
info.statement: In {location}, the mental health HPSA designation is {value}.

info.short_description: USDA rural-urban continuum code classifying counties from metro to rural (1–9).
info.long_description: USDA Economic Research Service Rural-Urban Continuum Code. Codes 1–3 are metropolitan counties (by population size of metro area); codes 4–9 are nonmetropolitan counties ranging from urbanized adjacent to metro areas (4) to completely rural or less than 2,500 urban population not adjacent to a metro area (9).
info.statement: In {location}, the rural-urban continuum code is {value}.

info.long_name: Non-Federal Medical Doctors in Total Patient Care
info.short_description: Count of non-federal MDs across all specialties in patient care roles.
info.long_description: Total number of non-federal medical doctors (MDs) in patient care roles across all specialties. Includes office-based, hospital-based, and other patient care settings. Does not include federal physicians or DOs. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} MDs in patient care.

info.long_description: Total number of non-federal MDs specializing in adult psychiatry (excludes child and adolescent psychiatrists, which are counted separately). Includes all activity categories (patient care, administration, teaching, research). Counties with zero psychiatrists are common in rural areas. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile compiled by HRSA.

info.short_description: Total number of hospitals in the county.
info.long_description: Total count of hospitals in the county across all types (short-term general, specialty, long-term, psychiatric, rehabilitation, and other). Source: American Hospital Association (AHA) Annual Survey compiled by HRSA.
Total county resident population from Census Bureau estimates as compiled by HRSA in the AHRF. For most editions, this reflects the most recent available annual intercensal or postcensal estimate.
info.statement: In {location}, the estimated total population is {value}.

info.short_description: County population density per square mile from Census data.
info.long_description: Resident population per square mile of total county area from decennial Census data compiled by HRSA. Values reflect the most recent available Census (typically 2010 or 2020 depending on the AHRF edition).
info.statement: In {location}, the population density is {value} persons per square mile.

info.short_description: Number of Medicare-certified critical access hospitals in the county.
info.long_description: Count of hospitals certified as Critical Access Hospitals (CAH) by CMS. CAHs are rural hospitals with 25 or fewer acute care inpatient beds, located more than 35 miles from another hospital, that receive enhanced Medicare reimbursement to maintain access to care in rural areas. Source: AHA Annual Survey compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} critical access hospitals.

info.long_name: Non-Federal Primary Care Physicians in Patient Care (Excluding Residents)
info.short_description: Count of non-federal primary care physicians (MDs and DOs) in patient care roles, excluding hospital residents.
info.long_description: Number of non-federal primary care physicians (including both MDs and DOs) actively in patient care, excluding hospital residents and those age 75 or older. Primary care includes general practice, family medicine, general internal medicine, general pediatrics, and obstetrics/gynecology. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile and CMS data compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} primary care physicians in patient care.

info.long_name: Dentists with Active National Provider Identifier
info.short_description: Count of dentists with an active NPI in the county.
info.long_description: Number of dentists with an active National Provider Identifier (NPI) in the county, derived from the CMS National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES). Includes all dental specialties.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} dentists with an active NPI.

info.long_name: Percentage of Days with Good Air Quality
info.short_description: Percentage of measured days rated 'Good' by EPA Air Quality Index.
info.long_description: Percentage of air quality monitoring days in the county rated 'Good' (AQI 0–50) by EPA's Air Quality System (AQS). Only counties with active monitoring stations have data; many rural counties report NA. Source: EPA AQS compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, {value}% of measured days had good air quality.

info.long_name: Annual Average Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Concentration
info.short_description: Annual average PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³) from EPA monitoring data.
info.long_description: Annual average ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentration in micrograms per cubic meter from EPA Air Quality System (AQS) monitoring data. In the ASCII editions, this is the average daily PM2.5 scaled by a factor of 0.01 (SAS implied-decimal format). Counties without monitoring stations may have NA values.
info.statement: In {location}, the annual average PM2.5 concentration is {value} μg/m³.

info.long_name: Actual Medicare Fee-for-Service Per Capita Expenditure
info.short_description: Actual Medicare FFS per capita spending for county residents.
info.long_description: Actual (not price-standardized) Medicare fee-for-service per capita expenditures for county residents enrolled in traditional Medicare. Reflects local healthcare prices, service intensity, and enrollment patterns. Source: CMS Medicare Claims data compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, Medicare FFS per capita spending is ${value}.

info.long_name: Emergency Department Visits per 1,000 Medicare FFS Beneficiaries
info.short_description: County ED visit rate among traditional Medicare fee-for-service enrollees.
info.long_description: Number of emergency department visits per 1,000 Medicare fee-for-service (FFS) beneficiaries residing in the county. Captures acute care utilization and may reflect access barriers, disease burden, or care coordination quality. Source: CMS Medicare Claims data compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} ED visits per 1,000 Medicare FFS beneficiaries.
info.unit: ED visits per 1,000 Medicare FFS beneficiaries

ahrf.name: Area Health Resource File (AHRF)
ahrf.description: The Area Health Resource File (AHRF) is an annual county-level database produced by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA). It aggregates data from over 50 sources including the AMA Physician Masterfile, the American Hospital Association Annual Survey, the Bureau of Health Workforce, CMS Medicare claims, the Census Bureau, and EPA air quality monitoring. The AHRF covers all U.S. counties and territories with measures of health workforce supply, health facility counts, demographics, socioeconomic conditions, health expenditures, and environmental factors. It is widely used in health services research to characterize county-level resource availability and identify shortage areas.
ahrf.restrictions: Public domain. HRSA data is produced by a U.S. federal agency and is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
